toad: Toad. An amphibian: it starts life as a tadpole in water and lives on land as an adult, eating insects.
owl: Barn owl. A night hunter: its dish-shaped face collects sound, so it can find a mouse in the dark.
co2: Carbon dioxide, C O 2,. A carbon atom between two oxygen atoms in a straight line, each held by a double bond. Plants use it to make food.
dolphin: Bottlenose dolphin. A mammal, not a fish: it breathes air through a blowhole and feeds its young on milk.
salt: Common salt crystal, N A C L,. Sodium and chloride ions take turns in a cube pattern; that is why grains of salt are tiny cubes.
prism: Triangular prism. Two triangle ends joined by three rectangles: 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices.
cactus: Cactus. A desert plant: its fat green stem stores water and makes food, and its leaves are spines that lose little water.
methane: Methane, C H 4,. Four hydrogen atoms round one carbon, pointing to the corners of a tetrahedron. It is the main gas in biogas.
cuboid: Cuboid. 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices, like a brick or a box.
uno: Arduino Uno board. A small computer for projects: its chip runs your code, and its 14 digital and 6 analog pins talk to sensors and motors.
shark: Blacktip shark. A fish with a skeleton of cartilage, not bone. It breathes through gills and smells blood from far away.
bunsen: Bunsen burner. A gas burner for the lab. Opening its air hole turns the yellow flame into a hotter blue one.
car: Obstacle-avoiding robot car. An ultrasonic sensor on a servo looks left and right, and the car turns away before it hits anything.
irsensor: I R obstacle sensor. An infrared L E D shines, and a receiver beside it looks for light bouncing back from something close.
cylinder: Cylinder. Two flat circular faces and one curved surface, like a tin. Volume = pi r squared h.
hemisphere: Hemisphere. Half of a sphere: one flat circular face and one curved surface. Volume = two thirds pi r cubed.
pyramid: Square pyramid. A square base and four triangles meeting at the top: 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices.
cube: Cube. 6 equal square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Faces + vertices minus edges = 2.
seaturtle: Green sea turtle. A sea reptile with flippers for legs. It swims thousands of kilometres to lay eggs on the beach where it hatched.
water: Water molecule, H 2 O,. One oxygen atom joined to two hydrogen atoms in a bent shape, at an angle of 104.5 degrees.
sunflower: Sunflower. Its big head is made of hundreds of tiny flowers, and each one becomes a seed.
servo: Servo motor, S G 90,. A small motor that turns to an exact angle, from 0 to 180 degrees, when the board tells it to.
microscope: Microscope. Its lenses make tiny things look hundreds of times bigger, like the cells of an onion peel.
l298n: L 2 9 8 N motor driver. Lets a small board run two big motors, setting their speed and direction with the batterys power.
cone: Cone. One circular face, one curved surface and one vertex at the top, like an ice-cream cone. Volume = ⅓pi r squared h.
robotarm: Robot arm. Four servo motors work as its base, shoulder, elbow and gripper, like a human arm that can pick things up.
linecar: Line-follower robot car. Two I R sensors under its front watch a black line on the floor and steer the car along it.
ammonia: Ammonia, N H 3,. A nitrogen atom with three hydrogens, shaped like a low pyramid. It is used to make fertilisers.
sphere: Sphere. One curved surface; every point on it is the same distance from the centre. Volume = four thirds pi r cubed.
body: Human body. All the main organs in their places, inside see-through skin. Tap any organ to hear its name.
hcsr04: Ultrasonic sensor, H C S R zero four,. One eye sends out a sound too high to hear, the other listens for its echo; the time taken gives the distance.
hexprism: Hexagonal prism. Two hexagon ends joined by six rectangles: 8 faces, 18 edges and 12 vertices.
kingfisher: Kingfisher. A small, bright bird that dives into water to catch fish with its long, sharp beak.
chameleon: Chameleon. A lizard that can change its colour, look two ways at once and catch insects with its long, sticky tongue.
